title: The country with a river in its name
subtitle: Why English says The Gambia, what the river has to do with it, and what a map cannot tell us.

sections.title: The article is part of the name

parts.text: The World Factbook calls the country The Gambia, while its capital is Banjul and its river is the Gambia River.
The word The is therefore part of the English country name, not an article added by a sentence or by this website.
That small word matters because Gambia is also the name of the river and because the country is often discussed beside Senegal, whose territory surrounds it on its landward sides.

sections.title: A country shaped by a river

parts.text: The country follows the lower Gambia River inland from the Atlantic coast. The river is not a border detail at the edge of the map: it is the long geographical feature around which the country is organised.
Banjul sits at the river's mouth, where the water reaches the Atlantic. The country's capital, its river and its internationally used name therefore appear together in a very small space.

sections.title: A narrow shape, a wide history

parts.text: On a map, The Gambia can look like a narrow corridor following the river through Senegal. That outline is often treated as a curiosity, but a shape on a map is the result of histories, negotiations and power rather than a natural boundary drawn by the river alone.

The short version of the story is easy to remember; the longer one needs the histories of Senegambia, European trade and colonial rule, and the people who lived along the river before and after those borders were made.

sections.title: What the name does not tell us

parts.text: A map name cannot tell us how people in The Gambia explain the name in Mandinka, Wolof, Fula or another language spoken there. It cannot tell us whether the name feels formal, ordinary, colonial, affectionate or simply practical in different settings.

This is where the documented record must stop and make room for people who live there. The next version of this story should be changed by those voices, not by guessing what the name means to everyone.
